name: read_file
description: Use this tool if you need to view the contents of an existing file.

filepath.description: The path of the file to read. Can be a relative path (from workspace root), absolute path, tilde path (~/...), or file:// URI

name: create_new_file
description: Create a new file. Only use this when a file doesn't exist and should be created. For a long file (more than a few hundred lines), write it in parts: create it with the first part, then call this again with append set to true for each further part. A call cut off at the output limit writes nothing, so smaller parts lose less.

filepath.description: The path where the new file should be created. Can be a relative path (from workspace root), absolute path, tilde path (~/...), or file:// URI.

contents.description: The contents to write to the new file

append.description: Add contents to the end of a file you already created, instead of creating it.

name: run_terminal_command
description:
Run a terminal command in the current directory.
The shell is not stateful and will not remember any previous commands.      When a command is run in the background ALWAYS suggest using shell commands to stop it; NEVER suggest using Ctrl+C.      When suggesting subsequent shell commands ALWAYS format them in shell command blocks.      Do NOT perform actions requiring special/admin privileges.      IMPORTANT: To edit files, use Edit/MultiEdit tools instead of bash commands (sed, awk, etc). A command that writes a file (redirection, Set-Content, node -e or python -c calling a write) counts as a file edit: use the edit tools for it, and if an edit was refused, the command is refused too.      Secrets in the host environment are not passed to commands; the person can allow a name in terminal.passEnv.      Choose terminal commands and scripts optimized for win32 and x64 and shell powershell.exe.

command.description: The command to run. This will be passed directly into the IDE shell.

waitForCompletion.description: Whether to wait for the command to complete before returning. Default is true. Set to false to run the command in the background. Set to true to run the command in the foreground and wait to collect the output.

name: file_glob_search
description: Search for files recursively in the project using glob patterns. Supports ** for recursive directory search. Will not show many build, cache, secrets dirs/files (can use ls tool instead). Output may be truncated; use targeted patterns

pattern.description: Glob pattern for file path matching

name: view_diff
description: View the current diff of working changes

name: read_currently_open_file
description: Read the currently open file in the IDE. If the user seems to be referring to a file that you can't see, or is requesting an action on content that seems missing, try using this tool.

name: ls
description: List files and folders in a given directory

dirPath.description: The directory path. Can be relative to project root, absolute path, tilde path (~/...), or file:// URI. Use forward slash paths

recursive.description: If true, lists files and folders recursively. To prevent unexpected large results, use this sparingly

name: create_rule_block
description:
Creates a "rule" that can be referenced in future conversations. This should be used whenever you want to establish code standards / preferences that should be applied consistently, or when you want to avoid making a mistake again. To modify existing rules, use the edit tool instead.

Rule Types:
- Always: Include only "rule" (always included in model context)
- Auto Attached: Include "rule", "globs", and/or "regex" (included when files match patterns)
- Agent Requested: Include "rule" and "description" (AI decides when to apply based on description)
- Manual: Include only "rule" (only included when explicitly mentioned using @ruleName)

name.description: Short, descriptive name summarizing the rule's purpose (e.g. 'React Standards', 'Type Hints')

rule.description: Clear, imperative instruction for future code generation (e.g. 'Use named exports', 'Add Python type hints'). Each rule should focus on one specific standard.

description.description: Description of when this rule should be applied. Required for Agent Requested rules (AI decides when to apply). Optional for other types.

globs.description: Optional file patterns to which this rule applies (e.g. ['**/*.{ts,tsx}'] or ['src/**/*.ts', 'tests/**/*.ts'])

regex.description: Optional regex patterns to match against file content. Rule applies only to files whose content matches the pattern (e.g. 'useEffect' for React hooks or '\bclass\b' for class definitions)

alwaysApply.description: Whether this rule should always be applied. Set to false for Agent Requested and Manual rules. Omit or set to true for Always and Auto Attached rules.

name: fetch_url_content
description: Can be used to view the contents of a website using a URL. Do NOT use this for files.

name: task_list
description:
Your task list: while planning, the steps of the work; while building, the list the plan gave you, to keep current. Send the complete list each time, in order.

Rules:
- Exactly one item is in_progress while you work. Mark an item in_progress before you start it and completed as soon as it is done, not in batches.
- Use blocked (with a note saying why) or cancelled instead of deleting an item that did not get done.
- Keep each item short and specific. Optionally give activeForm, a present-tense label shown while the item runs ("Running migrations").
- Repeat the id of items you keep. New items need no id. Completed items you leave out are kept. While planning, open items you leave out are removed and reset starts a new list; while building, open items you leave out are kept, so use cancelled to drop one.

The list is stored outside the conversation and sent back to you at the end of every request, so it survives compaction. The user can see and edit it; when they do, their version is what you get back.

items.description: The whole list, at most 50 items.

id.description: The item's id from the current list; omit for a new item

text.description: What to do, at most 200 characters

note.description: Why the item is blocked or cancelled

activeForm.description: Present-tense label shown while in progress

reset.description: Replace the list entirely, dropping completed items too. Use for unrelated new work.

name: present_plan
description:
Present your plan for the user's approval. Use it in Plan mode once you have researched enough to propose concrete work, instead of asking the user to switch modes.

It saves the plan as a markdown file in the workspace (.continuous/plans/<title>.md), makes its to-dos the task list, and shows the plan to the user, who can edit the file and then choose Build (start implementing) or keep planning. Stop after calling it: do not start implementing.

- title: a short name for the work.
- plan: the plan in markdown, for a person to read: the goal, the approach, the files involved, risks or open questions. Keep it short; do not repeat the to-dos.
- todos: the implementation steps in order, one short line each. They become the task list you update while you build.
- todo_details (optional): for a to-do that must wait for others, its `after` (the numbers of the to-dos it comes after); for one that a command can verify, its `check` (a command that exits 0 when the to-do is done and fails when the behaviour is wrong, such as a focused test run; not one that only checks that a file or a string exists); for one that needs a stronger or cheaper model than the rest, its `model` (the name of one of the user's chat models; a loop runs that to-do on it); its `files` (the files it changes, as paths or globs), so a loop can run to-dos that touch different files at the same time. Size each to-do as one reviewable change that one check can verify.
- decisions (optional): the choices left to the person: one they kept for themselves, or one a wrong answer makes costly (irreversible, security, cost, scope). Each has a self-contained question, two to four options, your pick, its type and the numbers of the to-dos that wait on it. A decision is not a to-do: it has no check and no status. Small choices are yours: decide them and write them in the plan as assumptions.

Calling it again with the same title replaces that plan file, so revise a plan by presenting it again.

title.description: A short name for the work, at most 120 characters. It names the file in .continuous/plans.

plan.description: The plan in markdown for a person to read: goal, approach, files involved, risks. Not the to-dos.

todos.description: The implementation steps in order, at most 50, each at most 200 characters.

todo_details.description: Optional. Per to-do: after (numbers of the to-dos it comes after), check (a command that exits 0 when it is done), model (the name of the chat model a loop runs it with) and files (the files it changes).

after.description: Numbers of the to-dos this one comes after

check.description: A command that exits 0 when this to-do is done and fails when the behaviour is wrong: a test run or an import that asserts a result, not a file-exists or grep check

model.description: The name of the chat model a loop runs this to-do with, instead of its usual one

files.description: The files this to-do changes, as paths or globs relative to the workspace; to-dos whose files do not overlap may run at the same time

budget.description: What this to-do may use, for example '25 turns, 200K tokens, 20 min': turns in one run, tokens and minutes over all its runs. A to-do that goes over is stopped and kept as it is. Optional

decisions.description: Optional. Choices left to the person, at most 5: each a self-contained question with options, your pick, its type and the to-dos that wait on it.

question.description: The choice, self-contained, at most 400 characters

type.description: What a wrong answer would cost

todos.description: Numbers of the to-dos that wait on this decision

name: hold_question
description:
Put a question in the person's inbox and keep working. They answer while work goes on; the answer reaches you now or a later run of this item.

- type: what a wrong answer would cost. access: something only the person can supply (a credential, a login, the output of something you cannot run). irreversible: deleting, publishing, migrating, anything hard to undo. security: credentials, permissions, exposure. cost: money or a large share of a budget. scope: what to build, add or drop. design: approach, library, architecture, interfaces, data flow. detail: naming, formatting, small defaults. A question on two of these takes the costlier one. Who answers depends on the type and the person's settings.
- kind "assumption" (the usual choice): you go on with the default you state in `assumption`. If the person overrules it, the item is redone.
- kind "blocking": only when there is no reasonable default. Do what you can without the answer, then call finish_item with outcome "waiting".
- options: two to four short choices when they exist, your default first.

Make the question answerable on its own, without this conversation: say what it is about, the options, and your default.

question.description: The question, self-contained, at most 1000 characters

type.description: What a wrong answer would cost

assumption.description: The default you are continuing with. Required for kind "assumption".

options.description: Two to four short choices, your default first

name: remind_me
description:
Save a note for a later run. Each item starts without this conversation, so what you do not save is gone. It is saved at once, so it survives a stopped run. Use it for what a later run would otherwise have to find again: a cause you tracked down, a command that works, a trap.

- when "item": for the run of the item numbered in `item`
- when "next_items": for the next item that runs
- when "retry": for a later run of this item (the default when `when` is left out)
- when "replan": for the next re-plan

Each reminder is delivered once. List in `files` the files it depends on: if they change before it is delivered, it arrives marked to check first.

note.description: What the later run needs, self-contained, at most 2000 characters

when.description: Which run it is for. Left out, it is "retry".

item.description: The number of the item in the plan. Required for when "item".

files.description: Paths of the files the note depends on, at most 10

name: finish_item
description: Report the item you were given and end your turn. This is the only way to end a turn: a turn that ends without it is not counted. outcome "done" when it is finished and its check, if it has one, exited 0 when you ran it; "waiting" when it needs an answer to a blocking question; "stuck" when you cannot finish it (say why in summary, and name what is in the way in `blocker`; when other work must come first, use blocker "dependency" and list it in `needs`: that is how you add a to-do you have just discovered you need); "later" when another item may settle it: the item comes back after the others, once, and needs `reminder`. A second "later" counts as stuck.

summary.description: One line: what you did, or why it is not done. At most 500 characters.

notes.description: Optional. What a later item should know: a command that works, a trap you hit. One or two lines, at most 300 characters; not progress.

blocker.description: With outcome "stuck": what is in the way. answer: only the person can say or supply it. observe: you cannot see what you need. plan: the item itself is wrong (too big, too vague). environment: a tool, credential or the machine. dependency: other work must be done first, named in `needs`.

needs.description: With blocker "dependency": up to 3 pieces of work that must be done before this item, each a short to-do. The re-plan puts them first.

reminder.description: Required for outcome "later": what you tried, what you learned, and why it may go better later. At most 2000 characters.

files.description: With outcome "later": paths of the files the reminder depends on

name: request_rule
description:
Use this tool to retrieve additional 'rules' that contain more context/instructions based on their descriptions. Available rules:
No rules available.

name: read_skill
description: Use this tool to read the content of a skill by its name. Skills contain detailed instructions for specific tasks. The skill name should match one of the available skills listed below:

skillName.description: The name of the skill to read. This should match the name from the available skills.

name: subagent
description:
Start a subagent: a fresh conversation with its own instructions and a subset of your tools, which works on one task and returns a single report. It does not see this conversation, so put everything it needs in the prompt. Only its final report comes back; its tool output does not.

Use one for broad searches or questions that need many files read when only the conclusion matters, or for independent pieces of read-only work. Do not use one for a single known file or a quick search you can do yourself, or for edits. Several subagent calls in one message run in parallel (at most 3 at a time). Subagents cannot start subagents.

Available agents:
- Explore: Fast read-only search of the codebase. Use it to find files, symbols and usages, or to answer a question that needs many files read, when only the conclusion matters. Say how thorough to be.

agent.description: Name of the agent to start, from the list above.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) label for the task.

prompt.description: The task, with all the context the agent needs and what its report should contain.

name: search_web
description: Performs a web search, returning top results. Use this tool sparingly - only for questions that require specialized, external, and/or up-to-date knowledege. Common programming questions do not require web search.

name: edit_existing_file

filepath.description: The path of the file to edit, relative to the root of the workspace.

changes.description: Any modifications to the file, showing only needed changes. Do NOT wrap this in a codeblock or write anything besides the code changes. In larger files, use brief language-appropriate placeholders for large unmodified sections, e.g. '// ... existing code ...'

name: single_find_and_replace
description:
Performs exact string replacements in a file.

IMPORTANT:
- ALWAYS use the `read_file` tool just before making edits, to understand the file's up-to-date contents and context. The user can also edit the file while you are working with it.
- This tool CANNOT be called in parallel with any other tools, including itself
- When editing text from `read_file` tool output, ensure you preserve exact whitespace/indentation.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable, for instance.

WARNINGS:
- When not using `replace_all`, the edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
- The edit will likely fail if you have not recently used the `read_file` tool to view up-to-date file contents.

filepath.description: The path to the file to modify, relative to the root of the workspace

old_string.description: The text to replace - must be exact including whitespace/indentation

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (MUST be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

name: grep_search
description: Performs a regular expression (regex) search over the repository using ripgrep. Will not include results for many build, cache, secrets dirs/files. Output may be truncated, so use targeted queries

query.description: The regex pattern to search for within file contents. Use regex with alternation (e.g., 'word1|word2|word3') or character classes to find multiple potential words in a single search.
